_source: MMG_v19_Client_Manual_Testing_Guideline_FG05-FG14_v1.0.xlsx / Testing Guideline, rows 15-29 (TC-DAT-016, TC-DAT-019, TC-DEP-001 ... TC-DEP-017)
_target: Odoo 19 only (the workbook describes the v19 deposit surface: account.payment.state is draft/in_process/paid/canceled/rejected, the per-partner deposit accounts are company_dependent JSONB columns rather than ir.property rows, and cancelling a sales order keeps its deposits attached)
_modules: account_partner_deposit 19.0.1.0.0 and sale_partner_deposit 19.0.1.0.0, branch staging_19 (mmg_19-custom). Every test probes for them and reports BLOCKED with an install instruction if absent.
_policy: All 15 cases are implemented for real. FG-06 needs no external system, so AUTOMATION_CONVENTIONS rule 4 requires no deviation for this suite (unlike FG-05, which had to be run against the Avalara sandbox). The two DATA cases (TC-DAT-016, TC-DAT-019) are whole-population reads that create and modify nothing; the thirteen TC-DEP cases build their own namespaced FG06 fixtures.
_no_cross_test_fixtures: The workbook chains almost every case onto the previous one (TC-DEP-005's precondition is 'TC-DEP-004 has passed', and so on). AUTOMATION_CONVENTIONS rule 5 forbids depending on another test's records, so each test builds the starting state its own precondition describes, at the totals the workbook's Test Data names, and asserts that state before touching anything. The registry order values 600-614 still reproduce the workbook's Order of Testing step 4.0 sequence exactly (TC-DAT-019, TC-DAT-016, then TC-DEP-003, 001, 004, 005, 012, 016, 006, 007, 009, 010, 011, 013, 017 LAST), so a full-suite run reads in the workbook's own order.
_onchange_is_asserted_not_simulated: The platform drives Odoo over /web/dataset/call_kw, the endpoint the browser uses. @api.onchange methods do not fire on create()/write() over RPC, but onchange(values, field_names, fields_spec) is a public method implemented in the web addon (addons/web/models/models.py:1973) and is exactly what a form view calls. tests/fg06/common.py::form_defaults reproduces opening a form (empty field_names = the create-from-scratch path) and onchange_values reproduces editing one field, so every workbook expectation of the shape 'the field fills itself in from the contact' is asserted against the same call the browser makes.
_safety: Fixtures are namespaced FG06 and swept before and after each test. sweep_fg06 sweeps deposits by their JOURNAL ENTRY's state, not the payment's: a remnant left by a refused Validate reads state='in_process' with a draft entry (BC-016), so a payment-state sweep would miss it; and v19's account.payment.unlink() calls button_draft() on the move and then unlinks it (addons/account/models/account_payment.py:957-959), so anything with a POSTED entry is excluded by the domain rather than left to fail - otherwise a confirmed deposit would be silently destroyed with its journal entry. cleanup() enforces the same refusal independently.

TC-DAT-019.reason: Read-only setup gate; the workbook says to run it before any other FG-06 case. Asserts both company_dependent deposit-account fields are readable, that the Invoicing tab really carries them, that a company-level default exists on both sides, and - for the WHOLE population rather than the workbook's ten samples - that every contact-level override resolves to an account that exists, is not deprecated, is reconcilable and has the account type the field's own domain demands. Adaptation: the workbook ticks values off a Novobi printout the platform does not hold, so the full inventory is written to TC-DAT-019-deposit-account-inventory.csv for the human tick-off and the printout comparison is logged as a RESIDUAL MANUAL STEP. Technical note: 'does this contact carry its own account?' cannot be answered by read() (which returns the effective value, silently falling back) nor by a '!= False' search (Field._field_to_sql resolves a company-dependent field to COALESCE(jsonb, fallback), so it matches every partner once a default exists) nor by ir.default._get_model_defaults (private, refused over RPC). It follows from Field.convert_to_column storing None when the written value equals the fallback (odoo/orm/fields.py:1000-1005): an override that equals the default is not stored, so 'carries its own' is exactly 'effective value != company fallback', which IS expressible as a domain. No SQL needed.

TC-DAT-016.reason: Read-only whole-population count and total for both deposit menus. The population is defined by reading each ir.actions.act_window's own domain at run time rather than retyping it, and the domains are themselves asserted, so a changed menu is reported instead of silently measuring something else. Totals are grouped by currency, because account.payment.amount is in each payment's own currency and one scalar total across a mixed population is not comparable to any baseline. Adaptation: the four baseline numbers are captured and reported (RESIDUAL MANUAL STEP) since the platform does not hold the Novobi figures, and the FG06 fixture share is subtracted so a tester does not see a false surplus from the suite's own leftovers - this is the only case in FG-06 that reads a whole-population figure. Invariants asserted without the baseline: the two populations are disjoint (a deposit on both menus would double the apparent liability), no live deposit has a blank Deposit Account, and three real non-fixture deposits open with every field the workbook names populated.

TC-DEP-003.reason: Full flow: the contact's Customer Deposit Account survives a reload (the company_dependent JSONB round-trip), a new deposit pre-fills from it through the real partner_id onchange, changing the contact changes the next deposit, and a vendor deposit pre-fills the VENDOR account with the customer field left untouched. That last assertion is the workbook's P0 shape - the customer account on a vendor deposit posts vendor prepayments into a customer liability account - and it is proven twice: on the form (onchange) and on a posted record. Adaptation: the workbook's 'two different customer-deposit liability accounts' are taken from the chart of accounts where two eligible ones exist (its own precondition says 'Novobi can point you at them'); where fewer exist a namespaced FG06 account is created rather than reporting BLOCKED, and which happened is logged. NOTE: the production half of this case is gated on MS-001, the ir.property -> JSONB migration script, which lives outside the module (account_partner_deposit/PORTING.md section 6 states 'TC-DEP-003 cannot pass in production without it'). This test covers the half that is testable from code; TC-DAT-019 is the case that catches a migration that did not run.

TC-DEP-001.reason: The four form behaviours plus the posting. Payment Type invisible and the required/conditional Deposit Account are asserted against the DEPOSIT form's arch resolved by its own XML id (not the generic payment form, which legitimately shows Payment Type); the pre-fill is asserted through the partner_id onchange; the status bar is asserted against statusbar_visible="draft,in_process,paid" and the state selection; and the journal entry must carry exactly one deposit-account line as a 2,500.00 credit plus one liquidity debit, with NO revenue line (the workbook's P0). Two findings this case surfaces rather than hides: (1) Expected Result line 3 says the record 'starts on Draft', but in v19 a saved unconfirmed deposit reads state='in_process' because _generate_journal_entry runs at create time for any payment carrying write_off_line_vals (addons/account/models/account_payment.py:1080) and every deposit carries them - that is BC-016, so the substance of the line is asserted against the JOURNAL ENTRY's state (draft before Confirm, posted after) and the in_process reading is logged with its source; (2) workbook step 6 says the Journal field offers only bank and cash journals, which is asserted against available_journal_ids - the field's actual binding - and v19 computes that over type in ('bank','cash','credit') (addons/account/models/account_payment.py:593-608) while the deposit action's own default_move_journal_types context key is read by no Python in v19, so on a database holding a credit-type journal with an inbound method this FAILS correctly and the log names the offenders and the decision for the Accounting Manager.

TC-DEP-004.reason: The whole four-screen journey driven through the same calls the buttons make: action_make_a_deposit, the order.make.deposit wizard, action_create_deposit, and action_post (the pop-up footer's Validate). The figure the workbook asks the tester to read 'before you validate' is read from the payment pop-up's own initial state, produced by onchange's first call over the act_window's context - so it is the number the pop-up would display, not a re-derivation. Asserts the button's visibility expression from the arch as well as the method working, because a method that works behind a hidden button is still a failure for the tester; the read-only Customer and pre-filled Deposit Account on the pop-up; Total Deposit 3,000.00 / Net Total 7,000.00; and a Deposits button of 1 whose count also proves the deposit's entry posted (deposit_ids gates on both states - BC-002 + BC-016).

TC-DEP-005.reason: 25 per cent of 8,000.00 must be OFFERED as 2,000.00 on the payment pop-up (read before Validate, as the workbook instructs), then Total Deposit 2,000.00 / Net Total 6,000.00, then a 0 per cent attempt refused with 'Deposit amount must be greater than 0'. The zero guard is in the wizard's action_create_deposit and fires before the percentage is converted (wizard/order_make_deposit.py:31-33), so it leaves no record - unlike TC-DEP-017's guard. The caption above the percentage input is recorded as an OBSERVATION and deliberately NOT asserted in either direction: the workbook states it is cosmetic and must NOT be raised, and DW-005 relabelled 'percentage' while keeping it a related='amount' alias because splitting it into two real fields is a wizard redesign rather than a port.

TC-DEP-012.reason: The case turns on which of two competing defaults wins: order.make.deposit.currency_id defaults to the COMPANY currency (wizard/order_make_deposit.py:18) while sale.order.action_make_a_deposit passes default_currency_id = the ORDER's (sale_partner_deposit/models/sale_order.py:69-73). Driving the real calls means the asserted currency is the one the override actually produced - if the field default won instead, the assertion fails, which is the workbook's 'amount that looks plausible'. Asserts the pop-up's Amount AND Currency before Validate, Total Deposit / Net Total in the order's currency, the currency on the deposit record, and that the journal entry carries both figures (amount_currency = foreign, debit/credit = company currency, which is the pair account_payment.py:80-89 builds). A foreign-currency order requires a pricelist because sale.order.currency_id is a stored compute with no readonly=False (addons/sale/models/sale_order.py:195-201); an FG06 pricelist is created, mirroring the module's own test fixture. BLOCKED (not FAILED) when fewer than two currencies are active or no usable rate exists - the workbook's own precondition, and without a rate _get_conversion_rate silently returns 1.0 and every figure would be meaningless while looking right. v19 has no group_multi_currency, so the check is the workbook's wording: count active res.currency rows.

TC-DEP-016.reason: Running Total Deposit / Net Total after each of three deposits (2,000 / 5,000 / 8,000 and 10,000 / 7,000 / 4,000), the percentage base, and a Deposits button of 3 listing exactly those three. On the percentage base the workbook does not assert which is correct - it says the percentage is taken on the ORDER total, adds 'Note which you see; Novobi needs to know', and its If It Fails says to report both figures and let Novobi decide rather than assuming a defect. The code reads order.amount_total (wizard/order_make_deposit.py:44), so this test asserts the workbook's stated expectation (3,000.00 on a 12,000.00 order) and, when the observed figure matches the remaining balance instead (1,750.00), logs BOTH numbers and the source line so the report Novobi asked for is in the evidence either way.

TC-DEP-006.reason: The three branches of action_view_deposit are asserted for what they return: res_id plus the deposit FORM view for one deposit, a domain naming exactly this order's deposits for several, and the button hidden by invisible="deposit_count == 0" for none. 'No deposit from another order appears' - the workbook's serious assertion - is checked in BOTH directions. Adaptation: the workbook's precondition inherits TC-DEP-004's and TC-DEP-016's orders and carries an explicit ordering warning (run after TC-DEP-016, before TC-DEP-017, which adds a fourth deposit and would change the count). Building all three orders in-test removes that hazard entirely rather than working around it, while the registry order value 608 still places the case between them for a full-suite run.

TC-DEP-007.reason: IMPLEMENTED WITH A DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE THE CLIENT SHOULD ACT ON. The workbook's steps are Create Invoice, Confirm, THEN expand Outstanding credits and click the deposit to apply it. On v19 the deposit is already applied when Confirm returns: sale_partner_deposit.account_move.action_post collects the order's deposit_ids and calls _reconcile_deposit -> js_assign_outstanding_line (models/account_move.py:7-17). Once applied the deposit fails the panel's own domain, which needs reconciled = False and a non-zero residual (account_partner_deposit/models/account_move.py:41-50); and before Confirm the panel is suppressed because the override returns early unless the move is posted (:32-37). So on an invoice raised FROM THE ORDER there is no moment at which the panel offers that deposit, and steps 3-5 cannot be performed in the order written. This is working code meeting a workbook written against the manual path - the STEP ORDER needs correcting, not a defect - and it is logged as a FINDING with its source lines. All of the workbook's outcomes are asserted on that path (7,000.00 due on a 10,000.00 invoice, partial payment status, the intermediate 'Deposit to Payment' entry posted in the company's Customer Deposit journal debiting the deposit account with no revenue line, and the deposit no longer fully available). Expected Result line 1 - 'the deposit appears in Outstanding credits for 3,000.00' - is a statement about the PANEL, so it is asserted where the panel is genuinely reachable: on a deposit the automatic application does not consume, with the workbook's own figures and through the same js_assign_outstanding_line the workbook's step 5 clicks. The absence of the word 'Deposit' in the panel labels is recorded as an OBSERVATION and deliberately not asserted - the workbook says it is expected and must not be raised (decision D3-a) - while the OWL payload keys ARE asserted, which is the BC-006 regression guard.

TC-DEP-009.reason: The acceptance test for BC-016. A confirmed 2,500.00 deposit must be offered on the customer's next 4,000.00 invoice (an empty panel there is a P0 per the workbook), a second deposit saved but NOT confirmed must NOT be offered, and no other customer's deposit may appear in either check - so a second FG06 customer with a confirmed deposit is created specifically to make that last line meaningful. The case works because a standalone invoice has no sale order behind it, so sale_partner_deposit's automatic application cannot fire and the panel is genuinely offered; that is asserted (the invoice is still fully due) rather than assumed. The unconfirmed deposit reads state='in_process' with a draft entry, and both states are logged so a reader sees why the panel's parent_state='posted' clause is what makes the workbook's expectation hold. 'Neither empty nor over-full' is asserted as both halves: the confirmed deposit is still offered after the draft one is added, and the entry count did not grow.

TC-DEP-010.reason: GATE 4 and the workbook's 'single most important FG-06 case'. Asserts the deposit-account line's DATABASE IDENTITY survives an edit, which is the point of decision D2-a: v19 stock deletes and recreates write-off lines on every synchronisation (addons/account/models/account_payment.py:1042-1045) and the deposit line IS the write-off line, so stock behaviour would change its id and orphan any partial reconcile - while the recreated line still carries the right amount. An amount-only assertion would therefore pass on the broken implementation, which is exactly the failure the workbook calls invisible on screen. The three-way outcome is implemented literally: the assertion is on the PAIR (Amount Due, is-the-deposit-offered) being one of the two shapes the workbook allows, with the forbidden applied-and-available shape named in the failure text and flagged as a GATE 4 stop. All four numbers the If It Fails column demands are recorded from a finally block whatever the outcome, because it says to state all four even if they look fine. Also the BC-017 regression guard: reset-to-draft reaches the payment through origin_payment_id, and the v15 name raised AttributeError here, breaking reset on EVERY invoice.

TC-DEP-011.reason: The mirror of TC-DEP-010, worked from the invoice side. Asserts the invoice returns to draft, the deposit still exists and is neither cancelled nor deleted (its absence is a P0 per the workbook) with its journal entry still posted, the intermediate 'Deposit to Payment' entry removed - which is what frees the deposit - and the freed 3,000.00 offered again in Outstanding credits on another invoice for the same customer, i.e. not stranded. On step 7 the workbook expects the full 10,000.00 due after re-confirming; because the invoice was raised from an order, re-confirming re-runs sale_partner_deposit's automatic application, so both outcomes are handled: the 7,000.00 shape is accepted with a logged explanation AND an assertion that the deposit is applied and not ALSO offered (no double count), while the 10,000.00 shape asserts the workbook's figure and that the deposit is still available. The workbook's conditional 'if TC-DEP-010 left the invoice fully due, redo TC-DEP-007 step 5' disappears because the starting state is built in-test - a branch removed rather than hidden.

TC-DEP-013.reason: The workbook has already corrected this case once (its Why It Matters says the old expectation of a reversed liability never happened in either version) and the port's record corrects it again: v15 detached deposits with order.deposit_ids = [(5, 0, 0)], but the 18.0 branch this port came from REMOVED that override and ships a test asserting the links are kept, so v19 leaves deposits attached to a cancelled order (sale_partner_deposit/PORTING.md section 4, which flags decision D5-a as needing to be re-taken). The workbook itself says the deposit may still show as attached and that this is agreed behaviour and NOT a defect (Expected Result note, If It Fails, Read Me change item 9), so the attachment is recorded as an OBSERVATION for that open decision and deliberately not asserted in either direction. What IS asserted is the whole substance: the order cancels; the deposit still exists, is still confirmed, its entry still posted and its deposit-account line still present (which also closes the CB-001 data-loss question by observation rather than documentation); it is offered in Outstanding credits on a new 1,500.00 invoice and applies normally; and that invoice ends fully paid with 500.00 of the 2,000.00 still unused.

TC-DEP-017.reason: Runs LAST, as the workbook's Order of Testing requires. Every attempt is checked twice - on the error raised and on the database afterwards - because the workbook's Why It Matters says the record that should not exist is the only visible evidence. Attempts of 5,000.00 (more than the 4,000.00 of room) and 20,000.00 (more than the order) must both be refused with a readable message, and attempt C of exactly 4,000.00 must be ALLOWED, since compare_amounts uses > 0 so equality passes; without attempt C a guard that rejected everything would look like a success, and its success is also the BC-001 regression guard (the guard reads amount_company_currency_signed; the v15 name it replaced raised AttributeError on every deposit post). IMPORTANT correctness note: the guard lives in action_post, and Validate is two requests - the deposit row is created and committed by one, and action_post rolls back only itself. A browser does the same, saving via web_save before calling the footer button. So a refused attempt can leave an UNPOSTED remnant. The test therefore splits the two shapes rather than reporting a false defect: a POSTED deposit of a refused amount fails the assertion (the guard did not stop the money, and per the workbook nothing is deleted so Novobi can see it), while an unposted remnant is reported as a separate data-hygiene FINDING with its cause, since no journal entry and therefore no liability stands behind it.
